title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 16 Jul to 21 Aug 2026
summary: From 16 Jul to 21 Aug 2026 the radar shows the lake shrinking from 33.83 km2 to 30.63 km2, or -9.5%. Part of this loss may be an error on 16 Jul, when 17.1% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: The lake changed by -3.2 km2 over 36 days. Mean HV moved by -0.1 dB and mean HH by 0.32 dB. In HH, 1.29 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 0.3 km2 darker; in HV, 0.49 km2 turned brighter and 0.34 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The open water type darkened by 0.42 dB in HH. Rough dry ground and fields had 0.52 km2 brighter in HH. The changing fields type rose 0.74 dB in HV, and built-up land rose 0.48 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause: shadowed slopes joined to the lake mask on 16 Jul, which would make the loss look larger than it was; the outlines on the map would show it. Possible cause: real summer drawdown; the dam's level record would confirm it. Possible cause for the darker water: a calmer lake surface on 21 Aug.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag, but the 16 Jul lake figure deserves care. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen. Lake areas are approximate: 17.1% and 10.4% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Do not report the 3.2 km2 loss without the dam's level record. Use a start date with less outline on land for a firmer drawdown figure.
